solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Set out in licit manner before onset of temptation prompting decision to break the law

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come before the next piece
to set something out is to lay it out afresh, so these letters are arranged anew
the onset of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tempting thought arrives in a perfectly lawful way, and suddenly someone resolves to commit a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' rearranges IN LICIT MANNER into CRIMINAL INTEN; 'onset of temptation' adds T. 'Prompting' simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the mental element of a crime is the deliberate purpose to commit it, a resolve to offend.

clue.text: First I nail it somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unstated way, an arrangement signal

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to start by hammering a nail in, in whatever way they can.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something at the very start of a sequence is the first of it.

clue.text: Edge part of foot

definitions.meaning: to edge is to move slowly and carefully, as a verb
a twelfth of the imperial length unit of twelve such measures

explanation.definitionFit: Edging along is creeping by small steps; and the imperial foot divides into twelve smaller units of length.

clue.text: Disney maybe having an alternative aim to bitter end

indicators.note: an alternative form of the word aim, its letters in another order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Walt Disney, perhaps, harbouring a different goal right to the sour finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' turns AIM into IMA; 'bitter end' gives R. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney is an example: he made cartoons, drawing characters that move on screen.

clue.text: Fit fashionable type

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a type or kind is a form

explanation.surface: A trendy sort of person who keeps in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a sportsman in good condition and playing well is said to be fit and on song.

clue.text: Patience as bit of land's turned over with earth to go on allotment

indicators.note: the earth letter goes on, that is precedes, the share that follows
turned over says the word for the plot is flipped end to end

parts.note: a lot is a plot or parcel of ground
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
an allotment is a portion handed out, a ration

explanation.surface: Gardening patience: a plot dug over and soil added on one's allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes TOL from LOT. 'allotment' is not the vegetable plot here but a share handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: forbearance or putting up with things, the patient tolerance of what one dislikes.

clue.text: Feed and grass mostly in garden centre

parts.note: to nurse a baby is to feed it

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: rye is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Plant food and lawn seed bought at a garden centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery raises and sells young plants, just as a horticultural retailer does.

clue.text: Scraps with unusual grit then butts

parts.note: something unusual is odd
grit is coarse sand
butts are stubs or ends, as of cigarettes

explanation.surface: Discarded bits: oddly gritty stuff and cigarette stubs, perhaps swept up from the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: miscellaneous leftover bits and pieces, small remnants of various kinds.

clue.text: One's taking host around greeting English following bad behaviour

indicators.note: the host's letters go around those for one's

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a show's host
one's read as I's, that is I is, gives IS
hi is a greeting
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone is escorting a host about, saying hello to an Englishman after some misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as 'I's', short for 'I is'. 'taking' is only a link; 'around' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: naughtiness or playful troublemaking, especially by children.

clue.text: Half out of luck and free to be melodramatic

indicators.note: half taken out of the word means its first two of four letters

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: Someone half out of luck and set loose, going over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sensational or shocking, as of lurid tabloid headlines or overblown drama.

clue.text: Company with floating assets run like Spar is legendary source of trouble

parts.note: P and O is a British shipping company, whose assets float
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
as means like
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: A ferry firm run like a grocery chain sounds like a recipe for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of British convenience stores, but here it means to box. P&O is a long-established British shipping and ferry line.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth: the jar Pandora opened released every evil into the world, so it stands for a source of many troubles.

clue.text: Dry run with outside help

indicators.note: with something outside means it is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: aid is help
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dry run, conducted with assistance from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: parched, with no moisture, as a desert climate.

clue.text: Cast raid sherry and they blow hot and cold

indicators.note: to cast is to shape or throw anew, so these letters are formed into new order

explanation.surface: Actors raid the sherry and turn moody and changeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they blow hot and cold' usually means people who keep changing their minds; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-held appliances for drying hair which blast warm or cool air.

clue.text: So-called random number put in order

indicators.note: so-called means what something is called, i.e. named aloud, a sound signal

parts.note: stray means random, stray bullets, and ten is a number

explanation.surface: A supposed random number that turns out to be put in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tidy up or arrange neatly, as one tidies a room or desk.

clue.text: Toiled away without energy adding new shelving

indicators.note: adding says the next letter is tacked on at the end
without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
away suggests the letters are knocked out of place and reordered

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A worker slaved away without any energy, but then new shelving was added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges TOILED into DELTIO, which goes 'without' (outside) E, giving DELETIO. 'Shelving' means setting aside, not shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelving a plan means dropping it, and a cut or striking out is the removal of something.

clue.text: Rejig working holiday and get stick

indicators.note: to rejig is to reorganise, here swapping the two parts round

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a stay is a visit or break away

explanation.surface: Someone reorganises a working holiday and then gets criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stick' looks like the British slang for being criticised, but only 'stick' is the definition; 'and get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remain somewhere rather than leave, as to stick at a job.

clue.text: Writer's less than boring and — how can I put this? — a swinger

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: less than the whole word, so a letter of it is dropped

parts.note: boring means dull
um is the hesitant sound of someone searching for words

explanation.surface: A writer is somewhat dull and, delicately put, sexually adventurous.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight hung from a fixed point that moves to and fro, as in a clock.

clue.text: Study more than once or about twice a day

indicators.note: twice says the word for about is written two times

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Studying again, or about twice daily.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over a text again, a second perusal of the same material.

clue.text: Loud note first? Quiet note first, that can be cool

indicators.note: first says the note goes ahead of the loud letter
first again puts the note ahead of the hush

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
re again, a sol-fa note
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A musician debates whether to play loud or soft first, in something that may be cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something fresh and cold, as a cold drink revives one.

clue.text: Combustible love god in mad keen embrace

definitions.note: used as a noun: a combustible is a substance that burns

indicators.note: embrace says the shuffled letters wrap around the god
mad suggests the letters are scrambled wildly

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Passion catches fire as Cupid is wrapped in a frantic, eager hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the letters of 'keen' into KENE. 'Combustible' looks like an adjective but works as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable fuel oil, paraffin in Britain, used in lamps and jet engines.

clue.text: Authorise returning soldiers to hold detainee

indicators.note: to hold means to contain the next piece within
returning says the corps' letters run backwards

parts.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British army corps
a POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Soldiers coming home are given authority to guard a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to give someone the power or right to do something, to license.

clue.text: With odd exceptions jazzy backing marks rise of marimba here and there in part of Africa

indicators.note: backing says those letters run backwards
with the odd-placed letters excepted, so only the even ones are kept

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
here and there picks letters at intervals, the even ones

explanation.surface: Jazzy backing tracks feature marimba flourishes in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: From JAZZY the even letters AZ are turned back to ZA; MARIMBA's even letters AIB rise to BIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked country in southern Africa, the former Northern Rhodesia.

clue.text: Tested watch's seconds machinery in case something goes wrong

definitions.text: machinery in case something goes wrong

parts.note: something tested and proven is safe
a watch is a guard, the possessive ending here being link padding

explanation.surface: A tested watch's second hand mechanism, in case it fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective measures or devices put in place to prevent harm or accidents.

clue.text: Portion of Christmas pudding for Charlotte perhaps

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of Christmas pudding set aside for a girl called Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is a link word: the answer cannot stand in for 'for Charlotte perhaps'. Charlotte is a potato variety, not a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a salad potato variety, and a potato is colloquially called by this short slang name.

clue.text: A good own goal will get you on the edge of your seat

definitions.text: on the edge of your seat

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A neat own goal will have football fans excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eagerly excited and expectant, waiting keenly for what happens next.

clue.text: Douglas's Trevor back in clear?

indicators.note: back says what remains of the name reads in reverse
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, whose Manx cats are tailless, so the name docks its tail

explanation.surface: A man named Trevor from Douglas is back in the clear.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas's Trevor is a Manx one: like a Manx cat it loses its tail, TREVO, and 'back' turns it into OVERT. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: open and not hidden, plain to see, the opposite of covert.

clue.text: Good old post-Fifties western with outlaw going round in costume

indicators.note: going round says the ban word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban

indicators.note: post means after, so good and old come after the fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: A good old post-1950s cowboy film with an outlaw riding around in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts BAN around LLGOW. 'Western' is not a film here, just W.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal dress worn by a woman at a grand dance, a special outfit.

clue.text: Unusual sight: a panorama that's a series of dreamlike images

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters appear in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A strange view: a wide vista that looks like a dream sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence of shifting, fantastic visions, as in a dream or an old magic lantern show.
